Component reference

Built for moments that matter.

This responsive reference distills the imported library’s core families and states. Every example uses measured Figma values for color, type, spacing, radius, and control sizing. Start with Atoms, Avatar, and Badges — the building blocks used across the rest of the catalog.

Primitives

Atoms

Shared containers that wrap an icon or split content. Use these instead of inventing a new circle or rule for each screen.

01 / 13

Icon plate

Icon container

A circular plate for a single glyph. Production sizes in the component set are 40, 48, 56, and 80. The inner placeholder scales 20 / 24 / 28 / 40. The page also documents 16, 24, 32, 64, and 160 as related image-container sizes — do not mix those into this plate unless a spec says so.

Divider

Two types: a 1px content rule, and an OR rule that splits a line around Body 2 Medium label. Reference width is 343px.

Content and OR
OR

Identity

Avatar

Circular identity for a member, provider, clinic, or the Dot assistant. Prefer a photo. Initials are the next fallback. Clinic and provider glyphs are for those roles when a photo is not available. Dot is reserved for the Included Health assistant.

02 / 13

Preferred

Photo

Crop a real photograph into the circle. 24 through 160. A verified badge may sit on 48 and up, bottom-right.

Sizes with optional verification

Figma sizes: 24, 32, 48, 64, 80, 160. Photo uses a 1px border/weakest ring. Verified overlay: 16 / 22 / 28 / 46 on 48 / 64 / 80 / 160.

Fallback

Initials

Use two letters when no photo is available. Neutral weak fill, black Figtree Bold. Type tracks the named scale: Caption at 24, Body 2 at 32, Title 3 at 48, Title 2 at 64, Title 1 at 80, Display 1 at 160.

AL across sizes
AL AL AL AL AL AL

Place

Clinic fallback

Location glyph on a neutral plate when the subject is a clinic or site, not a person. No verified badge. Sizes start at 32 — there is no 24 in the Figma set.

32 to 160

Assistant

Dot

The Included Health assistant mark on white with a weakest border. Do not substitute a member photo or initials for Dot.

24 to 160

Clinician fallback

Provider fallback

Use when initials are not available for a clinician. Neutral plate plus the exported person-medical glyph. Verified badge may appear from 48 up, as in the Figma matrix.

24 to 160

Annotation in Figma: provider fallback if initials are not available. Initials are used when no photo is available.

Status marks

Badges

Two families: a verified seal for Included Health or Doctor On Demand, and a notification mark for unread or unseen activity. Do not invent a third badge shape.

Credential

Badge Verified

Scalloped Included blue seal. Small is 32px; large is 44px. IH uses the knockout logomark. DOD uses the dr+ mark. Place on an avatar’s bottom-right — never as a standalone brand logo.

Actions

Buttons

Use one primary action per task. The family covers three hierarchy levels, two sizes, fixed or content-fit widths, destructive actions, and six interaction states, plus groups, icon buttons, text links, and the segmented control. Every button label is set in Body 1 — Figtree Medium 500 at 16 / 24.

Size, width, and intent

Button groups

Groups keep related actions on one decision. Stack vertically when both labels are long or the surface is narrow; pair horizontally when the two labels are short. The group holds one primary and one secondary — never two solid buttons.

Vertical, horizontal, and appointment groups

Vertical · 8px gap

Horizontal · secondary leads

Appointment times and CTA

Chips carry a Caption Bold time over a Footer date, sit at a 44px minimum height, and behave as a single-select radio group. The group's own action stays secondary so the chips remain the primary decision.

Icon buttons

Use an icon button only when the action is already obvious in context — dismiss, expand, more. Small is 32px with a 16px glyph, medium is 40px with a 20px glyph, and both keep a 48px tap region. Always supply an accessible name.

Colors and states · small, filled
Brand Neutral Destructive Default Hover Focus Pressed Disabled
Size and background

32px and 40px, each with and without the neutral background field.

Text links

Text links carry navigation inside a sentence or beneath a form — policy pages, benefit details, help articles. They share the button label style, Body 1 in Figtree Medium, and stay underlined so they read as links without relying on color alone.

States

DefaultTerms of Service

HoverTerms of Service

FocusTerms of Service

PressedTerms of Service

DisabledTerms of Service

Hover and pressed tint the 8px rounded field behind the label rather than changing the ink, so contrast never drops. The Figma specimen draws focus at 1px; it is rendered here at 2px to meet the WCAG 2.2 focus appearance minimum.

Segmented control

Use a segmented control to switch between two to four views of the same content — never to submit an action. The selected segment lifts onto a white field with a check and Body 2 Bold; the rest stay Body 2 Medium on the shared track.

Two, three, and four segments

Arrow keys move the selection and the 32px track keeps a 48px tap region. Keep labels to one or two words; below 600px the check is dropped and the white field alone carries selection so four segments still fit at 360px.

Choose the right feedback pattern

The source system distinguishes scope and initiation before visual style. Critical recovery actions must remain visible and should never rely on an auto-dismissing toast.

Placement and behavior
Page banner

System initiated. Communicates a page-wide or service state and scrolls with content.

Top · below navigation

Inline banner

System initiated. Explains section-specific content, consequences, or required context.

Adjacent to related content

Toast

Closes the loop after a member action. Keep it brief; allow dismissal or use a short timeout only when appropriate.

Bottom · above navigation

Data entry

Inputs & forms

Labels stay visible, fields are 48px with 8px corners, and focus uses a 2.5px Included blue ring. Required fields use an asterisk — never “optional.”

06 / 13

Content rules

Form info

Mark required field titles with an asterisk. Keep submit active. Use Skip when a screen is optional.

Required fields and actions
Required (*)

Place the asterisk at the end of the label, even when the screen has one field. Do not add a legend that explains the mark.

Optional questions

Do not label fields “Optional.” If the whole screen can be skipped, pair Continue with Skip or Not now.

Submit stays active

Do not disable the submit action. If a required value is missing, show an error after the member tries to continue.

Action language

Use continue and cancel for a single path forward. Use next and back in multi-step flows. Prefer enter over type.

Single line

Text field

Body 1 Bold labels sit 8px above a 48px field. Placeholder and value both use Body 1 Medium. Hints use Caption.

Structured content

Lists

Five production families from the Anatomy Lists page organize related choices, progressive detail, status over time, promotional benefits, and label–value information. Choose the family by task rather than styling every row alike.

08 / 13

Selection and navigation

List items

The base item is 88px high and composes optional leading media, Body 1 content, and one trailing control. Compact text-only lists use 64px rows; dividers span the content width.

Leading and trailing variants

Figma: 88px base row · 56px leading media · 20px checkbox/radio · 32–36px trailing action · 16px horizontal inset. Keep the entire navigational row clickable; use native controls for selection rows.

List templates
Care team

People supporting your care

Progressive disclosure

Accordion

An 80px header expands to reveal related supporting content. The same header returns to its original collapsed state; do not change its label or replace the disclosure control after opening.

Collapsed and expanded
What does my plan cover?

Your plan includes virtual primary care and support understanding your benefits. Review your plan details for service-specific costs.

How do I prepare for a visit?

Have your medications and questions nearby, and join from a private place with a stable connection.

Can I change my appointment?

Open the appointment from Activity to review available rescheduling and cancellation options.

Figma: 343px reference width · 80px header · 44px disclosure target · expanded examples at 152–168px total height. Native details preserves keyboard and screen-reader behavior.

Ordered status

Timeline

Use a vertical timeline only when order and status are both meaningful. Complete, in-progress, not-started, danger, time-dependent, and cancelled states combine a 22px marker with a solid or dotted connector.

Care request progress
  1. Request receivedToday · 9:14 AM
  2. Benefits reviewedYour coverage details are ready.
  3. Finding care optionsIn progressYour Care Team is reviewing available providers.
  4. Choose a providerNot started

Figma: 22px status dots · 12px dot-to-copy gap · solid connectors for established progression and dotted connectors where timing or transition remains open.

Benefit summary

Promo bullets

A short, scannable group pairs one supporting icon with one member benefit. Use parallel language and keep each explanation to one concise line when possible.

Why use Included Health
  • Care that fits your lifeConnect virtually or find trusted care near you.
  • Benefits made clearerUnderstand coverage and costs before you choose care.
  • Support in one placeMessage your Care Team when questions come up.

Use three to five bullets. Icons support recognition but never replace the visible text label.

Label and value

Detail List

Use a Detail List for compact, non-editable facts. Values may be plain text, text with an icon, a text link, or a status paired with a text link; dividers are optional when grouping is already clear.

Navigation

Six production patterns from the Anatomy Navigation page: persistent destinations, in-page views, and legal wayfinding. Do not mix a bottom tab bar with a web top nav on the same surface.

Authorship

Response

Dot speaks without a filled bubble; care-team replies use neutral fill; member replies use the weak brand surface. Every response uses Body 1 Medium.

Files

Attachments

Member and care-team files use the sender’s bubble surface. File rows are 56px high; image files may expand to a larger preview surface.

Single choice

Quick Reply

Quick replies use Body 2 Medium and 48px pill targets. Stack longer choices; use a horizontal row only when labels remain short.

Multi-select Reply

Compact 32px Caption chips allow more than one response. Selected options stay visibly filled; unavailable options use disabled semantics.

Symptoms

Safety context

Disclaimer

Keep the AI disclaimer near Dot’s conversation context and use Caption Medium centered within a 343px reading width.

Dot guidance

Dot can provide generalized AI-generated answers for select healthcare questions and connect you to the Care Team at any time, but it is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

Brand identity

Logos

Use the 2026 Included Health and Doctor On Demand lockups from Anatomy. Export the official files — do not redraw, recolor, or restack the mark and wordmark.

11 / 13

Brand logo

Horizontal lockups for Included Health (blue and knockout white) and Doctor On Demand. Use these at product and marketing scale; do not redraw the type or mark.

Style variants

Brand logo mark

Compact marks for tight chrome such as top nav and app icon contexts. Pair with the matching wordmark color: blue on light, white on Included blue.

Style variants

Logo example usage

Centered editorial presentations from the Anatomy examples frame: IH on white, IH knockout on Included blue, DOD on white, and the cobrand lockup.

Surfaces
Usage
IH / Blue
Primary lockup and mark on white or pale surfaces. Keep Included blue as drawn.
IH / White
Knockout lockup and mark on Included blue fields. Do not place white logos on white.
Doctor On Demand
Use the dr+ wordmark or mark for DOD surfaces. Keep the “by Included Health” tagline with the wordmark.
Cobrand lockup
Use the IH + DOD lockup when both brands must appear together. Do not rebuild the divider or restack the pair.

Disclosure and overlays

Patterns

Progressively reveal supporting detail and reserve modals for focused, interruptive decisions.

12 / 13
Accordion and modal
When should I use an inline banner?

Use one for contextual information that belongs to the current task and should remain visible while the member acts.

When should I use a toast?

Use a toast to confirm a completed action. Keep it brief and do not place critical recovery steps inside it.
